description:
The WHEN OTHER arm of EVALUATE EIBAID at app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl:99-102, driven by DFHPF12 - the invalid-keystroke path, and the REENTER half of gate G38. The EVALUATE at :93 has three arms in source order and this case pins the third: :94 WHEN DFHENTER, :96 WHEN DFHPF3, then :99 WHEN OTHER. Order is behaviour and WHEN OTHER must stay last, because it is the default rather than a fourth named key (G30). DFHPF12 is the byte that proves the default really defaults: common.CicsAid gives it 0x7C, it equals neither DFHENTER's 0x7D nor DFHPF3's 0xF3, and app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy would resolve it to a real key token - but COADM01C does not copy CSSTRPFY, so the arm is chosen by comparing the raw byte and every AID but the two named ones falls through to :99. A translation that branched on a resolved token instead would make some other key behave like PF3 in a program that has no such behaviour.

The arm does three things and this case pins all three. :100 MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG turns the error flag on. :101 MOVE CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY TO WS-MESSAGE loads the message, and the exact bytes are worth deriving rather than copying: app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:20-21 declares CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY PIC X(50) from a 49-character source literal, which is 40 characters of text followed by 9 spaces, so the VALUE right-pads it by one to the field's 50. Moving that PIC X(50) sender into the PIC X(80) WS-MESSAGE of :38 left-justifies and space-fills the remaining 30, so the eighty-byte image below is the 40-character text 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...' followed by exactly 40 spaces. It is declared on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel for that reason. Were the harness to surface the screen field instead, the :177 MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO narrowing into the PIC X(78) of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY:260 would keep the leading 78 - the same 40 characters plus 38 spaces - and that is a different channel, not a different rounding of the same one. Neither thank-you literal belongs anywhere near this case, and they are two literals rather than one: SystemMessages.CCDA_MSG_THANK_YOU is PIC X(50) and reads 'Thank you for using CardDemo application...', while ScreenTitles.CCDA_THANK_YOU is PIC X(40) and reads 'Thank you for using CCDA application...'. Different texts at different widths, owned by different copybooks - CSMSG01Y and COTTL01Y - and substituting either for the other, or for the invalid-key text, is a parity break rather than a typo.

:102 PERFORM SEND-MENU-SCREEN is the third thing, so the screen IS repainted: :175 BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS recomposes the four active lines, :177 moves the message to ERRMSGO and :179-184 sends map COADM1A of mapset COADM01 with ERASE. The four lines are rebuilt from app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy rather than echoed, each one :231's MOVE SPACES followed by :233-236's STRING of the PIC 9(02) option number, the two-character '. ' literal and the PIC X(35) name - 2 plus 2 plus 35 is 39, and because STRING does not pad, the fortieth character is the space :231 left there. OPTN005O to OPTN012O are the unpainted image at their declared PIC X(40): :228-229 iterates only to CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT, which the copybook fixes at 4, so lines 5 to 12 are never written at all. They are NOT the product of an output reset, and the distinction matters here: MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COADM1AO at :89 sits inside the IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER of :87 and is therefore first-entry only, so this REENTER path performs no reset of any output field.

Two things the arm does NOT do are pinned just as deliberately. It writes no colour. The only attribute byte COADM01C ever moves is the DFHGREEN of :148, on the coming-soon path this case never reaches, so ERRMSGC below is the mapset's own declared COLOR=RED at app/bms/COADM01.bms:154-157 - named by its BmsAttributes.DFHRED mnemonic rather than a raw byte, because colour is how the program distinguishes an error from a confirmation. There is no asterisk and no explicit DFHRED move, and there cannot be: the COPY list at :50-61 is COCOM01Y, COADM02Y, COADM01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA, CSSETATY is not among them - its only consumer in this migration is COACTUPC - and DFHRED appears zero times in the program's 268 lines. Expecting the CSSETATY highlight G38 is usually phrased around would be inventing behaviour. And it reads no option: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY is not performed on this arm, so :117-125 never run and :125's MOVE WS-OPTION TO OPTIONO never fires. The '1 ' the request supplies is therefore ignored as an input and comes back unchanged as the re-supplied image, which is why OPTIONO below is '1 ' and emphatically not the '01' the normalisation of :123 would have produced had the ENTER arm been taken. Statelessly there is no previous COADM1AO to preserve, so the field holding what the client sent is the faithful rendering of a field the program did not touch.

The communication area is handed back with not one field mutated. :100 to :102 touch working storage and the map, never CARDDEMO-COMMAREA; :88's SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER belongs to the first-entry branch this path did not take, and :141's MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT belongs to the transfer path it also did not take. So CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives 1 and leaves 1, all sixteen fields of the 160-byte area round-trip identically, and the transaction ends at :107-110's EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CA00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) - RETURN_TRANSID, with no successor named, which is why nextProgram is absent rather than blank. That the area is comparable at all is the whole of G37: the conversation state travels in the payload and there is no server-side session holding it. The adapter this case is dispatched to runs the invocation three times - twice on one service instance and once on a freshly constructed one - and requires all three outcomes to be equal, so the arm is pinned as deterministic as well as correct; a translation holding WS-ERR-FLG or WS-MESSAGE in a field of a shared bean would leak the first call into the second. Only the first outcome is reported, because one invocation produces one response. The unit is the service, constructed and called directly with no HTTP and no MockMvc in the path (G51), so the thirteen items below are precisely what it produces: the twelve menu lines and the option echo. TRNNAMEO, PGMNAMEO, TITLE01O, TITLE02O, CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are absent by design, because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO reads FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :204 and belongs to the controller if the service is to stay deterministic; ERRMSGO is absent because the eighty-to-seventy-eight narrowing of :177 is the controller's step. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant COADM01C's own version footer at :267 carries, so one clock governs every case in this directory, and US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default.

Every expected value above is statically derived: read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl, the PIC X(50) VALUE of app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy, the option table of app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy, the xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COADM01.bms. None of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from an execution of the legacy program. There is no COBOL execution baseline behind it: none was produced, and none could be produced in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from this repository, which is precisely why the AID and attribute mnemonics this case names come from common.CicsAid and common.BmsAttributes. Only the provenance of the expected values changes; the twenty cases per program, the field-for-field comparison and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand unchanged. Because provenance is a stated success criterion, the substitution is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than silently absorbed - risk R-A, as ParityHarness's class documentation states it.
